input: Compare mortgage refinancing rates from three lenders

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The type of refinance (rate-and-term vs. cash-out) and loan type (fixed vs. ARM, 15 vs. 30 year) completely changes which rates to look for and how to compare them.
The borrower's credit score, income, and existing equity directly affect which lenders are relevant and what rates they will qualify for.
The current loan balance and home value determine the LTV ratio, which is a core driver of the rate offered by any lender.
A deadline (e.g., rate lock expiry, financial urgency) or a hard limit on closing costs changes how aggressively and quickly the comparison needs to happen.
Whether the user wants to compare online quotes, work with a broker, or get formal Loan Estimates from lenders determines the entire method of gathering data.
The user may prioritize lowest interest rate, lowest APR, lowest closing costs, or lender reputation — these trade-offs lead to different recommendations.
Knowing what the final output looks like — a simple side-by-side table, a recommendation, or a full decision — defines how deep the comparison needs to go.

gold.taskTitle: Compare mortgage refinancing rates from three lenders
gold.taskDescription: Research and compare mortgage refinancing rates from three lenders to find the best option.

questions.title: What type of refinance are you pursuing?
questions.description: Determine whether this is a rate-and-term refinance, a cash-out refinance, or a specific product like an FHA streamline — this defines which loan products and rates to compare.

questions.title: What is your approximate credit score range?
questions.description: The borrower's credit score tier (e.g., 620–679, 680–739, 740+) is one of the biggest factors lenders use to set rates, so it determines which quotes are realistic.

questions.title: What is your current loan balance and home value?
questions.description: These two figures establish the loan-to-value ratio, which directly influences the rate tiers each lender will offer.

questions.title: Do you have a deadline or urgency driving this comparison?
questions.description: A time constraint — such as a rate lock expiring, a planned move, or financial pressure — affects how quickly quotes need to be gathered and whether speed outweighs thoroughness.

questions.title: How do you want to gather the rate quotes?
questions.description: Clarifies whether the user plans to use online rate tools, contact lenders directly, use a mortgage broker, or request official Loan Estimates — this determines the entire workflow.

questions.title: What matters most to you in a refinance offer?
questions.description: Identifies whether the user's top priority is the lowest interest rate, lowest APR, minimal closing costs, shortest break-even period, or lender trustworthiness — these trade-offs point to different winners.

questions.title: What should the final output of this comparison look like?
questions.description: Determines whether the user needs a simple side-by-side table of numbers, a written recommendation, a break-even analysis, or a full decision with next steps.
